Unit 4.8: The 10-Column Worksheet — From Adjusted Balances to Statement Columns

Organize adjusted balances without confusing a working paper with formal records.

Final Exam • Unit 4.8
Executive Summary: Worksheet Logic
Mara’s 10-column worksheet brings the unadjusted ledger, year-end adjustments and statement extensions onto one working paper. Its ₱529,308.00 adjusted trial balance still contains accounts that belong in different reports, so equal columns are only the starting check. Follow the salary accrual, inventory count and other adjustments before extending each net balance. The worksheet’s ₱33,132.00 profit bridges its SPL and SFP columns; formal statements and journal posting remain separate tasks.

Concept 1. Why Prepare a Worksheet

📌 Key Takeaway (Section 4.8.1)

A worksheet organizes five debit and credit pairs, but it does not replace the journal or ledger. Calculate each adjusted balance before extension, and follow every contra account’s own side. The entry Dr 105 Merchandise Inventory / Cr 350 Income Summary records ending inventory; beginning inventory leaves at closing.

Nica distinguishes cash from profit; Dario separates consumed supplies from the asset remaining.

Vignette 4.8-1: Dario’s Supply Count in PacoAdjustment to Extension

The Story: Dario sells desk organizers from a Paco market stall. His Supplies account has a ₱900.00 debit, but the December count finds only ₱300.00 unused; the missing ₱600.00 was consumed in the shop.

Which column? The consumed supplies belong in SPL debit, and the remaining asset belongs in SFP debit; the adjustment must also be journalized.

Vignette 4.8-2: Nica’s Container Stall in MalateProfit Bridge

The Story: Nica’s Malate container stall has ₱2,000.00 in SPL credit income and ₱1,400.00 in SPL debit costs. She has extended all account balances but has not entered the worksheet’s balancing profit.

Which side balances? Enter profit in SPL debit and SFP credit; the bridge balances the worksheet without posting another revenue entry.

Nica’s Container Stall
Profit Bridge — Worked Schedule
December 31, 2026
SPL credit income₱2,000.00
SPL debit costs1,400.00
Profit — SPL debit / SFP credit600.00
Balanced SPL total on each side₱2,000.00
  • Same side? Add. Debit plus debit increases a debit; credit plus credit increases a credit.
  • Opposite sides? Subtract. Deduct the adjustment from the old balance. If the adjustment is larger, the balance changes sides.
  • Extend the result, not the adjustment. Income and costs belong in SPL; assets, liabilities, capital and drawings belong in SFP.
  • Follow each contra account’s own side. ADA and accumulated depreciation go to SFP credit; contra-sales to SPL debit; contra-purchases to SPL credit.

Method 2. Extension Arithmetic and Opening Records

🔢 Computational Blueprint
1. Net each TB balance with its adjustment. 2. Extend income and expense balances to SPL. 3. Split beginning and ending inventory by destination. 4. Balance profit in SPL debit and SFP credit.

Start on January 1. These gross ledger balances represent the opening SFP; deduct the contra assets when reading net resources.

Inventory 4. Inventory Has Two Destinations

Record unsold ending goods as an asset now; remove beginning inventory through closing.

Keep the ledger method and the presentation bridge distinct

The ending adjustment is Dr Merchandise Inventory / Cr Income Summary. Before closing, 105 temporarily holds beginning plus ending inventory. Extend beginning inventory to SPL debit and ending inventory to SFP debit; extend the existing Income Summary credit to SPL credit.

The alternative worksheet bridge transfers beginning inventory out of the asset columns. It is not an additional journal entry: beginning inventory is posted at closing only.

  • Trace each account horizontally from ledger balance to statement destination.
  • Allowance and accumulated depreciation retain their own credit side in SFP; their associated expense debits belong in SPL.
💡 Why does the salary accrual credit a payable?

Staff earned wages, but payment has not occurred. The debit recognizes this year's staff services; the credit recognizes the unpaid obligation. Cash changes only when the business actually pays.

    💡 Does worksheet profit enter capital twice?

    No. The SPL and SFP balancing lines show the same profit from performance and equity viewpoints; neither is a journal entry.

    One result, two viewpoints

    SPL credits ₱282,960 − debits ₱249,828 = profit ₱33,132. Enter it in SPL debit and SFP credit, the smaller sides. SPL balances at ₱282,960; SFP balances at ₱279,480. These are worksheet balancing lines, not two journal entries.

    Proof 6. Read Each Row and Prove the Result

    Linen Kite is independent of the running ledger. Costs exceed income, so the loss fills SPL credit and SFP debit.

    • Cash stays put. No adjustment changes bank cash. The salary accrual recognizes work without payment: Salaries Expense increases and Salaries Payable becomes an outstanding obligation.
    • Insurance separates past from future. Subtract the adjusting credit from the prepaid debit. The remaining benefit goes to SFP; expired coverage goes to SPL as Insurance Expense.
    • An advance is not yet all income. The adjusting debit reduces Unearned Revenue. Its remaining credit stays in SFP; the earned portion joins Service Revenue in SPL.
    • Contra assets remain credits. Their related adjustment expenses go to SPL, but ADA and accumulated depreciation themselves reduce assets in SFP.
    • Split the inventory layers. Beginning goods form part of this year’s cost; unsold ending goods remain an asset. The two extensions must add back to the ATB debit.
    • Measure before balancing. Larger SPL credits mean profit; larger SPL debits mean loss. Place the difference on both smaller sides without changing account balances.
    Could an omitted salary adjustment leave the worksheet balanced?

    Yes. Both the expense debit and payable credit would be missing. Profit would be too high and liabilities too low even though the columns agree.

    Illustration 4.8-B: One Profit, Two Balancing PlacementsVisual Model
    Caption: Profit fills SPL debit and SFP credit; it is one result viewed through performance and equity.

    Errors 7. What Happens If Worksheet Adjustments Are Omitted

    Omitted wages understate expense and liabilities; misplaced inventory overstates assets. Equal columns cannot detect either classification error.

    Omission or ErrorConsequence
    Salary adjustment omittedExpense and liabilities understated; profit overstated
    Full inventory ATB extended to assetsBeginning inventory is retained instead of assigned to cost
    Whole drawing treated as expenseProfit understated; owner distribution misclassified

    Review 8. Common Traps & Exam Tips

    Check inventory destinations, Drawings and the profit bridge before accepting equal column totals.

    Trap 1: Check the Reporting Stage

    Sales is not SFP credit; drawings is not SPL expense; ADA is not SPL expense.

    Trap 2: Follow the Account’s Purpose

    The full pre-closing inventory debit is not ending inventory.

    Trap 3: Preserve Both Posting Sides

    Equality cannot reveal every omission.

    Trap 4: Reconcile the Result

    If interest were unpaid, accrue it; all notes interest is paid through year-end here.

    Units 4.9.1–4.9.3: Merchandising Statements — Profit, Equity & Financial Position

    Explain performance, owner capital and the resources and claims at year-end.

    Final Exam • Units 4.9.1–4.9.3
    Executive Summary: Merchandising Statement Connections
    Pebble Lantern reports ₱33,132.00 profit, but that amount is neither its cash increase nor its owner’s ending claim. The merchandising SPL explains sales, cost of sales and expenses; the SCOE combines performance with investment and drawings to reach ₱142,932.00 ending capital. The classified SFP then places that claim beside liabilities and ₱240,792.00 assets. Supporting notes explain the components behind the face statements, including net receivables and depreciated equipment.

    4.9.1.1 Read the Statement Chain

    📌 Key Takeaway (Section 4.9.1.1)

    Read the SPL, SCOE and SFP as a connected chain. Profit measures accrual performance, ending capital incorporates owner transactions, and the SFP reports resources and claims at one date. Cash receipts alone cannot explain any of those three reports.

    Entry shorthand: Profit to SCOE to SFP. The profit transfer changes the owner’s claim without creating another sale.

    A profitable sale and an owner’s withdrawal affect different reports even when both involve cash. Follow Lila’s sales margin and Rhea’s capital reconciliation before building Mara’s complete statement chain:

    Vignette 4.9.1-1: Lila’s Basket Sales in PandacanMerchandise Margin

    The Story: Lila’s Pandacan basket shop records ₱3,000.00 sales and ₱200.00 customer returns. The baskets sold cost ₱1,700.00; she still has shop expenses to deduct after finding merchandise margin.

    Which subtotal? Returns reduce sales before cost of sales is deducted; gross profit is not yet the final profit for the shop.

    The goods side

    Purchases − purchase returns and allowances − purchase discounts = net purchases. Add freight-in for net cost of purchases; add beginning inventory for goods available; subtract ending inventory for cost of sales. Freight-out is a selling expense.

    Classify Expenses By Their Use

    Allocate adjusted salaries, insurance and depreciation three-fifths to selling and two-fifths to administration; doubtful accounts expense is wholly administrative.

    4.9.1.2 Sales, Cost of Sales and Expense Functions

    🔢 Computational Blueprint
    1. Reduce sales for returns and discounts. 2. Add net purchases and freight-in to beginning inventory. 3. Deduct ending inventory for cost of sales. 4. Subtract operating and financing expenses to reach profit.

    Use the merchandising function form: incidental rent is operating, interest income investing and interest expense financing; no R&D or miscellaneous expense occurred.

    • Net sales less cost of sales gives gross profit. It measures the merchandise margin before selling, office and financing costs; a positive gross margin does not guarantee final profit.
    • Add other operating income. Wrapping fees and incidental store-space rent arise alongside shop operations. Use the facts rather than a universal rule for rent.
    • Deduct function totals once. Selling supports customers and distribution; administration supports the office and business as a whole. Transfer note totals to the face without repeating their detail.
    • Keep categories visible. Add investing income to reach profit before financing, then deduct financing expense. These are accrual performance categories, not cash balances.

    4.9.1.3 Formal SPL and Supporting Notes

    Start from January capital, add additional investment and final SPL profit, then deduct drawings. Investment is not income and drawing is not expense. Pre-closing Capital already contains investment: using it as opening capital and adding investment again would count it twice.

    • Customer returns and discounts reduce sales; the running case has neither, so net sales equals gross sales.
    • Note 2 adds beginning inventory and landed purchases, then deducts unsold ending goods before transferring cost of sales to the SPL.
    • Gross profit is merchandise margin before selling, office and financing costs.
    • Note 3 reports wrapping fees and incidental store-space rent as other operating income.
    💡 Does gross profit guarantee a final profit?

    No. Selling, administrative and financing expenses may exceed that margin. Gross profit does not yet include every cost needed to operate the shop.

    Check Resources And Claims
    • Receivables: deduct ADA from trade AR, then add the separate, fully collectible service accrual. Never deduct the allowance twice.
    • Use ending inventory and unexpired insurance; classify by expected use or earning date.
    • PPE: equipment cost less accumulated depreciation gives carrying amount. Gross equipment and net PPE are not two separate assets. Keep both ledger accounts.
    • Debt: current instalments remain current even when the original note was long term. Current and non-current portions must reconcile to Notes Payable.
    • Capital: use ending SCOE capital and verify assets = liabilities + equity. Equality alone cannot establish correct classifications.
    • The three-fifths allocation is a case fact, not a universal expense rule.
    • Allocate each charge separately; reconcile both portions to its adjusted total.
    • Rank each note after allocating costs.
    • Transfer only each note's total to the face of the SPL. Listing the detailed expenses again on the face would double-count them.
    💡 Does allocating depreciation create another expense?

    No. It divides the adjusted expense for statement presentation. The depreciation adjustment has already recognized the year's total cost allocation.

    Reconcile January capital plus investment and profit, less drawings; carry the result to SFP equity.

    Pre-closing capital already includes investment; adding that investment again would overstate equity.

    Illustration 4.9.1-B: Profit Flows Through Capital to Financial PositionVisual Model
    Caption: Transfer the final SPL result once to the SCOE, then carry ending capital to the SFP.

    4.9.3.1 Classified Financial Position

    • Use a point-in-time date for SFP resources and claims.
    • Net trade receivables for ADA; add fully collectible Accrued Revenue separately.
    • Report future insurance coverage as a prepaid asset. The remaining coverage is usable next year, explaining its current classification here.
    • Show equipment cost less accumulated depreciation in the supporting note. Cost and net carrying amount are two views of one resource, not two assets.
    • Use instalment dates to split Notes Payable between current and non-current portions.
    • Insert ending capital from the SCOE and compare the two sides. Total assets equal liabilities plus equity; equality alone cannot prove classifications correct.
    💡 Does a bank loan increase owner capital?

    No. Borrowing creates a liability rather than income or an owner contribution. Its cash effect is financing on the SCF; its unpaid balance is a liability on the SFP.

    Illustration 4.9.1-C: Resources and Their Financing ClaimsVisual Model
    Caption: Gross equipment and accumulated depreciation remain separate ledger accounts supporting one net resource.

    4.9.3.2 Read Subtotals and Reconcile Reports

    Transfer profit to SCOE and ending capital to SFP once each.

    4.9.3.3 What Happens If Statement Links Are Misclassified

    Investment entered as revenue overstates profit; deducting an allowance twice understates assets.

    Omission or ErrorConsequence
    Investment counted as incomeProfit overstated; owner funding loses its separate explanation
    Allowance deducted twiceReceivables and assets understated
    Pre-closing capital copied to SFPProfit and drawings have not reached the reported ending claim

    4.9.3.4 Common Traps & Exam Tips

    Check the capital transfer, net receivables and equipment note for duplicated amounts.

    Trap 1: Check the Reporting Stage

    Profit is not cash receipts.

    Trap 2: Follow the Account’s Purpose

    Keep contra-sales and contra-purchases in their own schedules.

    Trap 3: Preserve Both Posting Sides

    Do not classify every rent as investing, duplicate contra-asset deductions or use pre-closing capital on the SFP.

    Trap 4: Reconcile the Result

    All notes interest is paid through year-end in this case.

    Unit 4.9.4: Statement of Cash Flows — The Direct Method

    Classify receipts and payments by purpose, preserving signs and separating noncash acquisitions.

    Final Exam • Unit 4.9.4
    Executive Summary: Direct-Method Cash Reporting
    Pebble Lantern’s cash increase of ₱48,360.00 comes from three different sources of movement. The direct-method SCF reports customer and operating payments separately from equipment spending and owner or lender financing, then reconciles ₱68,400.00 opening cash to ₱116,760.00 ending cash. This pane traces the cash schedule, distinguishes gross receipts from net activity totals, and discloses equipment acquired by note without inventing a cash receipt or payment.

    4.9.4.1 Cash and the Purpose of the SCF

    📌 Key Takeaway (Section 4.9.4.1)

    The direct method classifies actual receipts and payments by operating, investing or financing purpose. Reconcile ending cash to the bank ledger and SFP; disclose noncash equipment separately.

    A bank deposit may be a collection from customers or new borrowing, and a payment may buy equipment rather than cover shop operations. Bela and Tomas identify the purpose behind each cash movement:

    Vignette 4.9.4-1: Bela’s Collections in ErmitaOperating Cash

    The Story: Bela’s Ermita wrapping booth collects ₱1,500.00 from customers and pays ₱900.00 to its paper supplier. The customer collections include old receivables, so they cannot simply be labelled this month’s sales.

    Which activity? Both movements are operating cash flows; their difference measures net operating cash, not accrual profit.

    Vignette 4.9.4-2: Tomas’s Cutter in Santa AnaInvesting and Financing

    The Story: Tomas borrows ₱2,000.00 for his Santa Ana craft shop, then pays ₱1,200.00 cash for a paper cutter. The lender’s deposit and the equipment payment appear separately on his bank statement.

    Which activities? Borrowing is financing and buying equipment is investing; netting them into operating receipts would hide how the cutter was funded.

    Cash includes money on hand and demand bank deposits. A cash-equivalent candidate must be short term, highly liquid, convertible to a known amount and exposed to insignificant value risk. A long-term deposit does not qualify just because it is a deposit. Pebble Lantern has only bank cash.

    The SCF helps investors assess distributions, lenders assess interest and principal payments, and management plan solvency, operating payments and future funding needs.

    Illustration 4.9.4-A: Gross Receipts and Payments by ActivityVisual Model
    Caption: Each bucket shows gross receipts and payments; the signed difference forms its net cash flow.

    4.9.4.2 Operating, Investing and Financing

    🔢 Computational Blueprint
    1. Add customer receipts and subtract operating payments. 2. Net cash investing receipts and acquisitions. 3. Net owner and lender cash movements. 4. Add all three signed subtotals to beginning cash.

    Classify an actual receipt or payment by the activity it finances or settles. A short-term loan still comes from a lender, while incidental shop-space rent belongs with this case’s operations.

    • O: customer and service receipts, incidental store-space rent; payments for goods, supplies, wages and operating costs.
    • I: buy or sell PPE, intangibles and other investments; advance non-trade loans and collect their principal.
    • F: owner cash investment and drawings, borrowing and principal repayments, including short-term loans.
    • The specific course rule: interest received and dividends received to I; interest paid and corporate dividends paid to F. A proprietor’s drawing is not a corporate dividend.
    Operating

    Operating cash flows come from customers and ordinary shop activities. Payments for goods, wages and insurance belong here even when the related accrual expense differs.

    Investing

    Investing cash flows concern long-lived resources and investments. Include the cash equipment purchase and interest received, while describing equipment acquired on credit separately.

    Financing

    Financing cash flows concern the owner and lenders. Include investment, borrowing, principal repayment, drawings and interest paid, including a short-term loan receipt.

    Illustration 4.9.4-B: Classify Purpose After Confirming CashVisual Model
    Caption: Current debt is still financing; the maturity label does not determine the activity.

    The bank cash tie

    ₱45,600 − ₱11,760 + ₱14,520 = increase ₱48,360. Add beginning cash ₱68,400 to obtain ₱116,760, exactly the TB and SFP bank cash.

    • A cash-flow statement explains a change in cash, so start with evidence of receipt or payment. An asset or liability change does not automatically prove a cash movement.
    • Ask whether cash actually moved this year. A credit sale creates a receivable rather than a cash receipt. A later collection supplies cash and reduces that receivable.
    • Find the exact cash amount. The supplier settlement includes a discount, so the payable reduction exceeds the payment. Use the net cash paid in the SCF; the journal records the complete settlement.
    • Identify what the transaction finances or buys. Collections for goods and wrapping services relate to operations. A cash equipment purchase acquires a long-lived asset and belongs to investing. Owner funding and borrowing change financing sources and belong to financing.
    • Apply the separate interest and dividend classifications. Interest received and dividends received are investing in these course examples. Interest paid and corporate dividends paid are financing. Mara's withdrawal is a financing drawing rather than a corporate dividend.
    • Preserve each flow's sign. Receipts increase cash; payments reduce it. A negative investing subtotal may simply mean that equipment was acquired for future use.
    • Exclude transactions without cash movement from all three cash totals. The equipment note increases equipment and debt together without changing cash. Describe it separately so readers understand the change in resources and borrowing.
    💡 Why is a short-term loan financing?

    Its nature is obtaining borrowed finance. The current label describes when the debt is due, rather than what the receipt represents.

    4.9.4.5 Cash Versus Accrual Performance

    Accrual profit includes earned revenue and consumed resources regardless of settlement date. The SCF instead follows money received and paid, so depreciation and changes in working balances explain why the two measures differ.

    • Read the verb. Collected, paid, borrowed and invested indicate possible cash events. A credit sale creates AR; collection later is the cash event.
    • Confirm the cash amount. A discount means supplier payment differs from the AP reduction. Accrual revenue and depreciation are not current cash flows.
    • Build operating first. Cash sales and credit-customer collections both supply cash; do not add credit sales themselves. Advance service receipts are operating even while unearned.
    • Use payments, not total expenses. Salaries earned can include unpaid work; insurance paid can include unused coverage. Neither equals its accrual expense automatically.
    • Separate I and F. Include equipment cash payments and interest receipts in I. Include owner funding, loan receipts, repayments, drawings and interest paid in F. Preserve inflow/outflow signs.
    • Add the three subtotals. Add net movement to opening cash and match the same-date TB and SFP. Cash can grow during a loss year because funding supplies cash.
    Separate mini-examples: operating cash is not profit

    Moss Cup’s receipts less supplier payments and wages yield operating cash, but more accrual information is needed for profit. Amber Mat then combines all three signed flows with opening cash. Both are fully worked in practice below.

    Is depreciation a direct operating cash payment?

    No. It allocates equipment cost without a current payment. Report the purchase when cash is paid; depreciation measures later accrual performance.

    4.9.4.6 What Happens If Cash Flows Are Misclassified

    A loan receipt placed in operations leaves total cash unchanged but misrepresents the source of liquidity. Including noncash equipment in both investing and financing is worse: it invents gross cash activity that the bank never recorded.

    Omission or ErrorConsequence
    Borrowing classified as salesOperating receipts overstated; financing receipts understated
    Supplier AP debit used as cash paidCash outflow overstated by the discount
    Equipment note included in cash totalsInvented investing and financing cash movements

    4.9.4.7 Common Traps & Exam Tips

    Use the bank movement to test whether a cash flow exists, then use its purpose to choose an activity. The notes and discount examples prevent balance-sheet labels from substituting for cash analysis.

    Trap 1: Check the Reporting Stage

    Loans are not sales; principal repayments are not expenses.

    Trap 2: Follow the Account’s Purpose

    Not every current liability belongs to operating: a short-term bank loan is financing.

    Trap 3: Preserve Both Posting Sides

    Credit purchases and noncash acquisitions stay outside cash totals.

    Trap 4: Reconcile the Result

    Unpaid interest would require accrual accounting, but all notes interest is paid here.

    Unit 4.10: Closing Entries — Clearing Temporary Accounts Through Income Summary

    Post the four steps and trace the balances that clear and continue.

    Final Exam • Unit 4.10
    Executive Summary: Closing Entry Logic
    Pebble Lantern has already measured December profit when closing begins; closing now prepares the ledger for another year. Credit-balance temporary accounts and debit-balance costs pass through 350 Income Summary, whose existing inventory credit also contributes to ₱33,132.00 profit. That result reaches Capital before Drawings closes directly to the owner’s claim. The worked journals and posting explorer show why temporary accounts finish at zero while ₱142,932.00 Capital and permanent balances continue.

    4.10.1 Temporary and Permanent Accounts

    📌 Key Takeaway (Section 4.10.1)

    Closing entries reset temporary accounts after statements are prepared. Use the opposite side to clear each existing balance, transfer the result to Capital, and close Drawings directly to Capital. Permanent resources, obligations and contra assets continue into the next period.

    Entry shorthand: Dr Income Summary / Cr Owner, Capital. A credit result in Income Summary increases Capital when transferred.

    A revenue balance must be cleared through Income Summary, while a personal withdrawal bypasses that performance account. Alon and Celia use small closing journals to expose the difference:

    Vignette 4.10-1: Alon’s Revenue Close in TondoStep 1

    Which closing step? Step 1 debits Sales Revenue and credits Income Summary; the existing revenue credit is cleared by its opposite side.

    4.10.2 Four Closing Steps in Order

    📌 Key Takeaway (Section 4.10.2)

    Clear each temporary account on its opposite side; Drawings closes directly to Capital because an owner distribution is outside profit.

    Pebble Lantern closes credit balances first, then debit balances, then Income Summary and finally Drawings. The sequence collects performance before transferring the net result, while keeping owner withdrawals out of profit.

    Accounting Sequence
    1
    Clear Credit Balances
    Debit revenues and credit-balance cost reductions.
    2
    Clear Debit Balances
    Credit expenses, costs and beginning inventory.
    3
    Transfer Result
    Move profit or loss to Capital.
    4
    Close Drawings
    Debit Capital and credit Drawings directly.

    • Temporary accounts measure activity for one reporting period. Their balances must be available to prepare the SPL and explain capital changes. Closing then resets those accounts for next year.
    • Complete adjustments first. Salaries must include unpaid December work before closing. Service Revenue must include completed work not yet collected.
    • Prepare statements from the adjusted balances. Closing too early removes the separate revenues and expenses needed for the SPL. The worksheet remains useful as a record of pre-closing balances.
    • Record and post the closing entries. A journal entry changes the ledger only when it is posted. The next TB comes from the updated ledger, not an unposted journal.
    • Retain permanent balances for the next period. Cash, equipment and obligations still exist when the calendar turns. Annual performance measurement does not make them disappear.
    • Compare ending Capital with the SCOE. Closing transfers an already measured result to the owner's ledger account. It does not calculate another year's profit.
    💡 Does closing salary expense settle the payable?

    No. Closing clears expense against Income Summary. The separate payable remains because staff are still owed cash. Payment later clears that obligation.

    4.10.4 Loss and Contra-Account Examples

    A net loss changes the direction of the Income Summary transfer, while sales returns and purchase discounts follow their own existing balance sides. Closing clears those balances without changing the underlying performance already reported.

    A loss reduces Capital

    Linen Kite’s loss requires a debit to Capital and credit to Income Summary. This clears a debit remainder.

    LINEN KITE SHOP • GENERAL JOURNALPAGE GJ-1

    Dec 31Owner, Capital3016,620.00
    Income Summary3506,620.00
    (To transfer the debit remainder in Income Summary as a loss that reduces Owner, Capital)
    Contra-sales are debit balances

    • Bamboo Dish’s sales returns and discounts close in step
    • Its purchase returns and discounts close in step 1, as shown in practice.

    BAMBOO DISH SHOP • GENERAL JOURNALPAGE GJ-1
    Date (2026)Account Titles and ExplanationP/RDebit (₱)Credit (₱)
    Dec 31Income Summary3502,790.00
    Sales Returns & Allowances4021,860.00
    Sales Discounts403930.00
    (To close sales returns and sales discounts to Income Summary on their opposite side)
    • The four steps group accounts by their balances and closing roles. The order lets Income Summary collect the result before transfer.
    • Locate Sales Revenue and the other income accounts in the ATB. Each credit needs an equal debit to become zero.
    • Locate Purchase Returns & Allowances and Purchase Discounts. They have credit balances because they reduce acquisition costs. Debit each in the same step as other credit-balance temporary accounts.
    • Add the debits and credit Income Summary for their total. This includes cost reductions as well as income. It is therefore not simply the SPL revenue total.
    • Include any Sales Returns & Allowances and Sales Discounts. They reduce sales but carry debit balances. Bamboo Dish illustrates these credits separately because Pebble Lantern has no contra-sales.
    • Credit only beginning inventory in Merchandise Inventory. The pre-closing ledger includes both beginning and ending layers in our method. Closing the full debit removes goods still on hand.
    • Post both sides and compute the remaining Income Summary balance. Include its existing ending-inventory adjustment credit. Ignoring that credit overstates the cost assigned to goods sold.
    • Read the balance after the first two steps and inventory adjustment. A credit remainder means profit; a debit remainder means loss.
    • For profit, debit Income Summary and credit Owner, Capital. The debit clears the temporary credit and the capital credit increases equity.
    • For loss, debit Owner, Capital and credit Income Summary. The credit clears the temporary debit and the capital debit reduces equity.
    • Check Income Summary after posting. It must now be zero even in a profitable year. Profit is retained in Capital rather than in the clearing account.
    • Keep Income Summary out of this entry. A personal distribution is an equity change rather than a business cost. Routing it through Income Summary understates business profit.
    💡 Why does closing credit a debit-balance account?

    The credit removes its existing debit for the new year. Normal balance describes how it accumulates activity; closing uses the opposite side to clear it.

    4.10.5 Prepare, Post and Retain the Right Balances

    The ledger must retain ending inventory and updated Capital after every temporary balance is cleared. Preparing statements first preserves the period’s activity detail before closing resets the revenue and expense accounts.

    • Finish adjusting. Include December unpaid salaries and completed uncollected service revenue. Prepare reports while separate revenue and expense balances still exist.
    • Post, do not merely write. An unposted journal leaves the ledger unchanged. Post every source account as well as Income Summary.
    • Include the inventory credit already present. Add step 1 credits, deduct step 2 debits and read the remainder. A credit means profit only at this intermediate stage. Step 2 can outweigh credits and produce a loss.
    • Clear the remainder. Step 3 gives Income Summary the opposite posting; total debits then equal total credits. Matched before/closing amounts show source temporary balances are zero.
    • Keep the drawing separate. Its Capital debit reduces equity without reducing profit. Salary expense closes, but staff remain owed their unpaid salaries.
    CheckpointProfit yearLoss year
    Summary after steps 1–2Credit remainderDebit remainder
    Clear SummaryDebit SummaryCredit Summary
    Capital effectCredit increases equityDebit reduces equity
    Drawing entryDr Capital / Cr Drawings
    Summary after completionZeroZero

    Scan revenue, expense, purchases and contra accounts for balances; confirm Drawings and Income Summary clear; match inventory to the count and Capital to SCOE; retain payables and permanent contra assets. Capital can still be wrong when all temporary accounts clear if earlier entries were omitted or misstated.

    • Scan revenue, expense and periodic purchases accounts for remaining balances.
    • Inspect contra-sales and contra-purchases individually.
    • Confirm Drawings and Income Summary are cleared.
    • Compare inventory with the physical ending count.
    • Reconcile Capital to the SCOE.
    • Retain outstanding payables and permanent contra assets.

    💡 Can closing transfer an incorrect recorded result?

    Yes. Earlier transactions or adjustments may have been omitted or misstated. Closing transfers the recorded result; it cannot prove earlier records complete.

    4.10.6 What Happens If a Closing Entry Is Omitted

    Failing to close Drawings preserves a debit that should have reduced Capital, while closing the whole inventory balance destroys a resource still on hand. Closing accuracy depends on the account being cleared, not merely on equal journal sides.

    Omission or ErrorConsequence
    Drawing close omittedTemporary drawing remains and capital is too high
    Full inventory debit closedUnsold ending inventory is removed
    Only Summary side postedSource revenue and expense accounts remain open

    4.10.7 Common Traps & Exam Tips

    Inspect the source balances after posting each closing step, especially Inventory, Income Summary and Drawings. A destination balance can look plausible while an unposted source account remains open.

    Trap 1: Check the Reporting Stage

    Do not close contra assets, route drawings through Summary, debit Capital for profit or credit it for loss.

    Trap 2: Follow the Account’s Purpose

    A Summary credit means profit only before transfer.

    Trap 3: Preserve Both Posting Sides

    Never repeat a beginning-inventory posting already made by another procedure.

    Trap 4: Reconcile the Result

    All notes interest is paid through year-end here.

    Unit 4.11: Post-Closing Trial Balance — Proving the Permanent Accounts

    Check ledger equality and account types after every closing entry is posted.

    Final Exam • Unit 4.11
    Executive Summary: Permanent Account Checks
    After Mara posts the closing journals, the post-closing trial balance extracts only the accounts that carry into the next period. It retains ₱29,700.00 inventory, contra-asset credits, outstanding obligations and ₱142,932.00 Capital, while revenues, expenses, Drawings and Income Summary disappear. This pane distinguishes the ledger’s gross debit-credit presentation from the SFP’s net classifications. A balanced schedule still needs reconciliation: omitting both sides of a closing entry can preserve equality while leaving the wrong accounts open.

    4.11.1 Purpose, Timing and Permanent Balances

    📌 Key Takeaway (Section 4.11.1)

    A post-closing trial balance is prepared after closing is posted and before January reversals. Equal columns test arithmetic, while account-type checks test whether closing is complete. Keep separate contra-asset credits and use ending inventory and updated Capital.

    Entry shorthand: 111 Accrued Revenue. The receivable remains collectible after Service Revenue has closed.

    Closing removes completed-period activity rather than every credit balance. Ivo’s remaining receivable and Sela’s omitted drawing close show why both account identity and column equality matter:

    Vignette 4.11-1: Ivo’s Remaining Claim in BinondoPermanent Balances

    The Story: After closing his Binondo stationery kiosk, Ivo still has ₱2,500.00 Cash, ₱500.00 Accounts Receivable and ₱700.00 Accounts Payable. His revenue account has cleared, but the unpaid customer balance remains collectible.

    Which accounts remain? Cash, the receivable, the payable and Capital remain; closing revenue does not cancel the customer’s debt.

    4.11.3 Same Position, Different Presentation

    The SFP presents useful net resources and grouped claims; the post-closing trial balance proves separate ledger balances. Different totals can therefore be correct when the difference comes from legitimate contra-asset presentation.

    ComparisonAmount
    Post-closing capital₱142,932.00
    SFP capital142,932.00
    Post-closing inventory29,700.00
    SFP inventory29,700.00
    Gross TB debit total₱268,080.00
    Net SFP assets₱240,792.00
    • The TB debit total is gross; SFP assets are net. The SFP deducts the allowance and accumulated depreciation, groups the accrual with receivables, groups salary payable with AP, and splits Notes Payable by maturity. These presentation changes do not create extra resources or separate ledger debts.
    • The post-closing TB checks balances after closing has been completed. It is not another SPL and does not measure a new result.
    • Confirm the date and stage of the cycle. Use December balances after all four closing steps have been posted. Exclude January transactions and reversals from the year-end schedule.
    • Read each permanent ledger account's remaining balance. A debit asset goes in Debit; a credit liability or Capital goes in Credit. Use the actual balance rather than assuming a side from the title alone.
    • Retain the contra assets as separate credits. Allowance for Doubtful Accounts and Accumulated Depreciation have not been closed. They support the net carrying amounts in the SFP.
    • Use only physical ending merchandise inventory. The beginning layer was transferred through Income Summary during closing. Carrying the full pre-closing amount overstates next year's opening inventory.
    • Use Capital after profit and drawings were transferred. Pre-closing Capital does not yet include all year-end equity changes. Compare the posted balance with the SCOE rather than copying the earlier TB.
    • Exclude all temporary accounts. Do not list Sales Revenue, Purchases, expenses, Drawings or Income Summary. Investigate any remaining balance before accepting the schedule.
      • 💡 Why does accumulated depreciation remain after closing?

      Depreciation Expense measures this year's equipment use and is temporary. Accumulated Depreciation records cost allocated across years and reduces the remaining asset. Its continuing credit is a permanent contra-asset balance.

    • Locate gross Accounts Receivable in TB Debit. Locate the allowance separately in TB Credit. The SFP deducts it and includes the separate Accrued Revenue asset in the receivables group.
    • Locate Store Equipment in TB Debit. Locate Accumulated Depreciation in TB Credit. The SFP combines them into the net PPE carrying amount.
    • Locate the single Notes Payable ledger credit. The SFP divides it into current and non-current portions using maturity facts. The split changes presentation rather than combined debt.
    • Compare Capital directly across reports. Both use the permanent ending capital after profit and drawings. It must agree even though other captions are grouped differently.
    • Explain why TB debits exceed net SFP assets. Gross asset debits appear without subtraction of contra-asset credits. The SFP asset total already reflects these deductions. The difference is presentation rather than an extra resource.
      • 💡 Should the trial balance replace equipment with net PPE?

      No. The TB lists actual equipment and accumulated-depreciation balances separately. Net PPE is a statement presentation supported by those two accounts.

    4.11.4 Balanced Does Not Mean Correct

    • Omitting an entire balanced entry can leave equal debit and credit totals. The omitted drawing close is especially easy to spot from the account list.
    • Suppose the whole drawing-closing entry was omitted. The drawing debit remains; the capital debit that should reduce equity is absent.
    • Inspect the account titles. Drawings is temporary and does not belong on a proper post-closing TB. The arithmetic test passed but the content test failed.
    • Record and post the missing closing entry. Debit Capital and credit Drawings for the existing drawing balance. Prepare a fresh post-closing TB from the corrected ledger.

    4.11.5 Reconcile and Inspect the Account Types

    Trace Accrued Revenue to the December adjustment and Capital to the completed closing transfers. Neither an unfamiliar account name nor a credit balance is sufficient reason to remove an account from the schedule.

    • Reconcile the gross and net views. AR less ADA plus Accrued Revenue gives the SFP group. Equipment less accumulated depreciation gives PPE. Never replace gross equipment in the TB with net PPE while retaining its contra account.
    • Match the direct links. Capital and ending inventory agree with SCOE/SFP without netting. The single Notes Payable balance equals current plus non-current debt.
    • Imagine the entire drawing close omitted. Drawing debit remains and the Capital debit is absent. Excess Capital credit offsets the drawing debit, so the totals can still agree.
    • Correct the ledger. Dr Capital / Cr Drawings for the unclosed amount, post both sides, then prepare a fresh TB. Equality by itself did not establish completed closing.
    Error equality can missWhy it balancesInspect
    Salary adjustment omittedBoth sides missingUnpaid staff records
    Equipment charged to expenseEqual postings to wrong accountInvoice and asset register
    Wrong amount on both sidesEntry still balancesOriginal source document
    Wrong customer accountTotal AR unchangedSubsidiary customer records
    Drawing close omittedDrawing offsets excess CapitalAccount types and SCOE
    💡 Why Accrued Revenue Remains After Closing

    Accrued Revenue is a receivable asset, despite the word revenue. Service Revenue measures period income and closes. Likewise, accumulated depreciation carries prior cost allocations while Depreciation Expense closes.

    4.11.6 What Happens If Temporary Balances Remain

    An omitted drawing close can leave the post-closing columns equal and Capital too high. A surviving revenue account gives a different warning: completed-period performance has not been cleared from the opening ledger.

    4.11.7 Common Traps & Exam Tips

    A final scan should find permanent accounts only, with contra assets still separate and Capital agreeing to the owner’s statement. Equal columns are necessary but cannot establish those conditions.

    Trap 1: Check the Reporting Stage

    Do not copy the ATB unchanged, remove credit contra assets or carry beginning-plus-ending inventory forward.

    Trap 2: Follow the Account’s Purpose

    A temporary account on a balanced schedule fails the content test.

    Trap 3: Preserve Both Posting Sides

    All notes interest is paid here; an unpaid interest accrual would remain a liability.

    Unit 4.12: Reversing Entries — Selected First-Day Mirrors

    Keep prior-year accruals and new-period cash recording in their proper periods.

    Final Exam • Unit 4.12
    Executive Summary: Reversal and Settlement Logic
    January bookkeeping can use a reversal to clear a December accrual before routine cash recording. Pebble Lantern reverses ₱2,760.00 accrued salaries and ₱2,220.00 accrued service revenue, then records settlement without counting the old-year amounts again as January performance. Comparing both settlement routes proves the same ₱5,520.00 January salary expense. Asset-method insurance and liability-method advances retain their adjusted balances; the separately labelled enrichment explains why alternative initial methods require different reversal decisions.

    4.12.1 Why Reverse Selected Adjustments

    📌 Key Takeaway (Section 4.12.1)

    A reversing entry mirrors a selected adjustment on the first day of the next period. It simplifies routine cash recording without changing December performance. Read the original method before deciding: Pebble Lantern retains asset-method prepayments and liability-method advances.

    Entry shorthand: Dr Salaries Payable / Cr Salaries Expense. This first-day salary entry clears the old payable before the routine payday debit.

    A January payment may contain December wages, whereas prepaid insurance already represents a measured resource at year-end. Mila’s payroll and Oren’s insurance illustrate when a mirror entry helps and when it would undo the opening balance:

    Vignette 4.12-1: Mila’s First Payday in MakatiAccrual Reversal

    The Story: Mila’s Makati label shop accrued ₱300.00 December salaries. She reverses the accrual on January 1, then records the full ₱900.00 January payday as Salaries Expense and Cash, including the old unpaid wages.

    Reverse or not? Reverse the salary accrual if using the routine full-expense payday entry; its January credit offsets the old-year portion of that debit.

    Mila’s Label Shop
    Accrual Reversal — Worked Schedule
    January 8, 2027
    January payday expense debit₱900.00
    January reversal credit (deduct)300.00
    Net January salary expense₱600.00
    Vignette 4.12-2: Oren’s Insurance in Quezon CityAsset Method

    The Story: Oren’s Quezon City frame stall recorded ₱1,200.00 insurance as a prepaid asset. By December 31, ₱400.00 has expired and was adjusted to expense, leaving ₱800.00 that still protects the stall next year.

    Reverse or retain? Retain the asset-method adjustment; reversing it would restore the expired portion to Prepaid Insurance and overstate the opening resource.

    Oren’s Insurance
    Oren’s Frame Stall
    December 31, 2026
    Original prepaid insurance₱1,200.00
    Expired insurance (deduct)400.00
    Opening prepaid asset to retain₱800.00

    Reversal simplifies the payroll or receipts clerk’s routine recording. It is optional bookkeeping, and its January date preserves December’s adjusted profit while changing the route used for later settlement.

    Illustration 4.12-A: Accrual, Reversal and Payday Across the Cut-OffVisual Model
    Caption: December work stays in December; reversal and payment together leave only January work in January expense.

    4.12.2 Decide From the Original Recording Method

    🔢 Computational Blueprint
    1. With reversal: debit the full payroll to expense. 2. Offset the January reversal credit for old-year wages. 3. Without reversal: debit the old payable separately. 4. Both routes leave only new-year work as January expense.
    📌 Key Takeaway (Section 4.12.2)

    Reverse accruals on January 1; retain asset-method insurance and liability-method advances at their adjusted opening balances.

    Ask: is this an accrual? If yes, reverse. If it is a deferral, inspect the original cash entry: expense-method prepayments and income-method advances can reverse. Asset/liability methods retain their adjusted balances. Depreciation, doubtful accounts and inventory do not reverse.

    Follow The Decision Tree

    What kind of December adjustment are you examining?

    The eight cards cover accruals, both deferral methods, depreciation and doubtful accounts. Closing inventory is also not reversed: its ending balance must carry forward.

    Accrued RevenueAccrued Revenue; RevenueRevenue; Accrued Revenue
    Accrued expenseExpense; PayablePayable; Expense
    Prepaid expense — expense methodPrepaid asset; Expense (unused part)Expense; Prepaid asset
    Unearned revenue — income methodRevenue; Unearned Revenue (unearned part)Unearned Revenue; Revenue
    Prepaid expense — asset methodExpense; Prepaid asset (used part)Do not reverse
    Unearned revenue — liability methodUnearned Revenue; Revenue (earned part)Do not reverse
    DepreciationDepreciation Expense; Accumulated DepreciationDo not reverse
    Doubtful accountsDoubtful Accounts Expense; Allowance for Doubtful AccountsDo not reverse
    Closing inventoryMerchandise Inventory; Income SummaryDo not reverse

    Pebble Lantern reverses salaries and Accrued Revenue. Its insurance used the asset method and its advance used the liability method, so those stay intact. Depreciation, allowance and inventory also remain.

    4.12.5 Alternative Methods and the Exact Mirror

    The enrichment cases begin with expense-method prepayments or income-method advances, unlike Pebble Lantern. Their year-end reclassifications explain why reversal choices cannot be copied from Mara’s asset and liability methods without reading the original entry.

    Enrichment: Alternative Expense and Income Methods

    These separate Saffron Shelf examples explain the alternative methods. The course method for Pebble Lantern is asset recording for prepayments and liability recording for advances; do not add these entries to Mara’s ledger.

    Saffron Shelf uses methods absent from Mara’s ledger. For a payment initially expensed, restore unused coverage at year-end and reverse that adjustment. For a receipt initially credited to income, remove the unearned part and reverse that adjustment. Mirror only the adjusting amount, never the original payment or receipt.

    4.12.6 Keep Dates, Methods and Settlement Together

    Keep the December adjustment, January reversal and final settlement on their actual dates. Backdating the reversal would remove the accrual from the very period whose performance the adjustment was meant to measure.

    • Locate December’s adjustment. Accrued expense was Dr Expense / Cr Payable; January mirrors it. Accrued Revenue was Dr Receivable / Cr Revenue; January mirrors it.
    • Read the method. An expense-method adjustment restored unused coverage; an asset-method adjustment recorded coverage consumed. An income-method adjustment removed an unearned portion; a liability-method adjustment recognized an earned portion. The original entry determines reversal.
    • Do not undo continuing measurement. Accumulated depreciation, allowance and ending inventory support next year’s opening resources. Reversing them would remove required carrying balances.
    • Compare net January expense. The reversal route temporarily credits expense, then debits the full payment. Without reversal, clear the payable and debit expense only for new work. Both routes preserve December wages in December.
    • Payment is still due. A reversed payable does not eliminate the economic obligation. The shortcut changes the recording route, not what staff earned or what cash is paid.
    Illustration 4.12-B: The Mirror Changes the Recording RouteVisual Model
    Caption: The reversal does not cancel the economic obligation or the need to pay employees.

    4.12.7 What Happens If a Reversal Uses the Wrong Method

    Reversing asset-method insurance removes a valid opening asset measurement, while backdating a salary reversal erases December expense. Method and date controls protect different parts of the cut-off and must both be satisfied.

    Omission or ErrorConsequence
    Asset-method prepaid adjustment reversedRequired opening asset measurement is undone
    Payment debit read without reversal creditOld-year wages are counted again in January expense
    January reversal backdated to DecemberThe adjusted prior-year result is undone

    4.12.8 Common Traps & Exam Tips

    For every proposed reversal, identify the original method, the adjustment’s accounts and the January settlement route. The first-day mirror is useful only when those three pieces remain consistent.

    Trap 1: Check the Reporting Stage

    Do not reverse all adjustments, change the amount or reverse the original cash transaction.

    Trap 2: Follow the Account’s Purpose

    Closing clears temporary accounts at year-end; reversing selected adjustments begins the new period.

    Trap 3: Preserve Both Posting Sides

    Reversal does not change December profit.

    Trap 4: Reconcile the Result

    Pebble Lantern has no unpaid interest accrual to mirror on January 1 because its notes interest was settled through December 31.

    4.12.9 In-Pane Formative Drills

    Identify the recording method before choosing a reversal, then combine the first-day mirror with settlement. The enrichment computations use different initial methods, while the salary exercise asks for January cost rather than the full cash payment.

    Step 2 Compute the 13 Adjustments

    🎯 What you produce · Unit 4.7

    One computation and one adjusting entry for each item, all dated December 31, 2026.

    1. Classify the item first: accrued expense, accrued revenue, prepaid expense, unearned revenue, supplies, depreciation, allowance or inventory. The type tells you which two accounts move.
    2. Compute only December’s amount. For notes, count days (360-day year, exclude the issue date) or months (12-month year).
    3. Write the entry with the debit first, then the indented credit, then a short explanation.
    4. Note which function each expense belongs to (selling, administrative or financing). You will need this for the SPL in Step 5.
    Expenses split between functions

    Depreciation Expense - Furniture, Insurance Expense, Rent Expense and Utilities Expense are shared: 60% selling and 40% administrative. Record each as one account in the ledger and split it only on the SPL.

    Step 3 Complete the 10-Column Worksheet

    🎯 What you produce · Unit 4.8

    A worksheet whose five column pairs all balance, with profit of ₱30,475.00 for December.

    1. Trial balance columns: copy the unadjusted TB and confirm both totals are ₱1,387,350.00.
    2. Adjustments columns: enter each Step 2 entry on its accounts. New accounts (payables, receivables, expenses, Income Summary) go below the TB. Total both columns: they must agree.
    3. Adjusted TB: for each row, combine the TB and adjustment amounts. Same side: add. Opposite sides: subtract and keep the larger side.
    4. Extend each balance. Revenues, expenses, contra-sales, purchases, freight-in, contra-purchases and Income Summary go to the SPL columns. Assets, contra assets, liabilities, capital and drawings go to the SFP columns.
    5. Merchandise Inventory has two destinations: its ATB balance (₱251,000.00) is beginning plus ending inventory. Extend the beginning ₱118,600.00 to SPL debit and the ending ₱132,400.00 to SFP debit. Income Summary’s ₱132,400.00 credit goes to SPL credit.
    6. Find profit: SPL credit total − SPL debit total = ₱661,800.00 − ₱631,325.00 = ₱30,475.00. Add it to the smaller column of each pair (SPL debit and SFP credit). Both pairs must then balance.

    Step 4 Journalize and Post the Adjusting Entries

    🎯 What you produce · Units 4.7–4.8

    The worksheet adjustments recorded formally in the general journal and posted to each ledger account.

    The worksheet is only a working paper. The ledger changes only when you journalize and post the adjustments.

    1. Copy each adjustment from the worksheet into the general journal in the same order, dated December 31.
    2. Post every line to its ledger account and write the account code in the P/R column only after posting.
    3. Recompute each ledger balance. Every balance must equal its Adjusted TB amount on the worksheet.

    Step 5 Prepare the Statement of Profit or Loss and Its Notes

    🎯 What you produce · Unit 4.9.1

    A function-form SPL (IFRS 18 categories) ending in profit of ₱30,475.00, supported by notes.

    1. Write the three-line heading: business name, statement title, and For the Month Ended December 31, 2026.
    2. Build Note 1 (net sales) and Note 2 (cost of sales) first. Their totals feed the face of the statement.
    3. Sort every expense by function. Split the four shared expenses 60/40. List each note’s expenses from highest to lowest.
    4. Place items by category. Operating: sales, cost of sales, rent income from the store space, selling and administrative expenses. Investing: interest income on the note receivable. Financing: interest expense on the note payable.
    5. Check: the profit on the SPL equals the profit on the worksheet.
    Splitting a shared expense

    Rent Expense ₱30,000.00 → selling ₱18,000.00 (60%) and administrative ₱12,000.00 (40%). Do the same for insurance, utilities and furniture depreciation. The two parts must add back to the ledger balance.

    Step 6 Prepare the Statement of Changes in Owner’s Equity

    🎯 What you produce · Unit 4.9.2

    Ending capital of ₱631,500.00, ready to carry to the SFP.

    1. Start with capital at the beginning of the period (the TB capital, since there were no new investments in December).
    2. Add the SPL profit. A loss would be deducted instead.
    3. Deduct drawings. Drawings never go on the SPL: they are a withdrawal by the owner, not an expense.

    Step 7 Prepare the Statement of Financial Position and Its Notes

    🎯 What you produce · Unit 4.9.3

    A classified, report-form SFP where total assets of ₱876,000.00 equal liabilities plus equity.

    1. Use a point-in-time heading: December 31, 2026 (not “for the month ended”).
    2. List current assets in order of liquidity. Group Accounts Receivable (net of the allowance), the note receivable and the interest receivable as trade and other receivables.
    3. Report Merchandise Inventory at the ending count, never the beginning balance.
    4. Show property and equipment at cost less accumulated depreciation in a note, longest useful life first.
    5. Classify liabilities. The 90-day note, the accruals and the remaining five months of unearned rent are all due within twelve months, so all are current.
    6. Bring in ending capital from Step 6, then check that both totals agree.

    Step 8 Journalize and Post the Closing Entries

    🎯 What you produce · Unit 4.10

    Every temporary account at zero and capital updated to the SFP amount.

    1. Step 1: debit every credit-balance temporary account (revenues, purchase returns, purchase discounts). Credit Income Summary for the total.
    2. Step 2: credit every debit-balance temporary account (sales returns, sales discounts, purchases, freight-in, all expenses) and the beginning Merchandise Inventory. Debit Income Summary for the total.
    3. Step 3: Income Summary now holds the profit as a credit balance. Debit Income Summary and credit Capital.
    4. Step 4: debit Capital and credit Drawings.
    5. Post, then confirm that Income Summary, every revenue and expense, and Drawings are zero, and that Merchandise Inventory shows only the ending ₱132,400.00.

    Step 10 Journalize and Post the Reversing Entries

    🎯 What you produce · Unit 4.12

    Reversing entries dated January 1, 2027 for the accruals only.

    1. Go through the adjustments one by one and ask: was this an accrual? Accrued expenses and accrued revenues are reversed.
    2. Prepaid expenses recorded as assets and unearned revenue recorded as a liability are not reversed. Neither are depreciation, the allowance or the ending inventory.
    3. Each reversing entry is the exact mirror of its adjustment: same accounts and amounts, debit and credit swapped, dated the first day of the new period.
    Show the decision for each adjustment
    AdjustmentTypeDecision
    (a) Consignment commissionAccrued expenseReverse
    (b) Interest on a note payableAccrued expenseReverse
    (c) Unpaid salariesAccrued expenseReverse
    (d) Interest on a note receivableAccrued revenueReverse
    (e) Prepaid advertisingPrepaid expense (asset method)Do not reverse
    (f) Prepaid insurancePrepaid expense (asset method)Do not reverse
    (g) Office supplies usedSupplies (amount used given)Do not reverse
    (h) Store supplies on handSupplies (amount on hand given)Do not reverse
    (i) Unearned rentUnearned revenue (liability method)Do not reverse
    (j) Depreciation of store and office equipmentDepreciationDo not reverse
    (k) Depreciation of furnitureDepreciationDo not reverse
    (l) Doubtful accountsAllowance (percent of receivables)Do not reverse
    (m) Ending merchandise inventoryInventory (periodic)Do not reverse

    Why reverse?

    When the ₱25,500.00 salaries are paid on January 5, the bookkeeper can simply debit Salaries Expense and credit Cash. The reversal already put a ₱25,500.00 credit in the expense account, so January ends up with no December salary in it.

    Step 11 Check Good Form Before You Submit

    🎯 What you produce · All units

    Work that is correct and presented the way an accountant would present it.

    • Every statement has a three-line heading: business name, statement title, date or period. Period statements say “for the month ended”; the SFP says “as of” a date.
    • Peso signs appear on the first amount of each column and on every total.
    • A single rule appears above each subtotal, and a double rule below each final total.
    • Every line has a label, and amounts line up in their money columns. Negative presentation uses parentheses.
    • The worksheet profit, SPL profit, SOE profit and Income Summary closing amount are the same number.
    • Ending capital on the SOE, the SFP and the post-closing TB is the same number.
    • Ending inventory appears on the SFP and the post-closing TB; beginning inventory appears only in the cost of sales note and closing step 2.
    • Only accruals are reversed, and the reversing entries are dated the first day of the next period.
    A final reminder

    Use this case to learn the method. Your group project has its own facts, accounts and amounts, so work through each step with your own data.

    Official Formula Guide Key Reminders

    Executive Summary: Finals Method Reminders
    • Worksheet: Net each account before extending; profit fills SPL debit and SFP credit.
    • Inventory: Dr Merchandise Inventory / Cr Income Summary records ending inventory; transfer beginning inventory once at closing.
    • Closing: Clear credit balances, debit balances, Income Summary and Drawings in order.
    • Reversing: Accruals reverse; asset-method insurance and liability-method advances remain intact.
    • Cash flows: Interest received is investing and interest paid is financing in these course examples.
